comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @vvo, @Jerskouille and @redox to be potential reviewers

> That's so cool @JanPetr. Should we bundle every single analytics service in its own widget to avoid writing again and again the same code?

Oh just saw the discussion in #1616. As you guys think 👍

Thanks @redox.
That's what we decided to omit (https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/1616#issuecomment-263539378). It'd require maintaining those services APIs in instantsearch.js and would become pain in future.
Because of that we settled on exposing only `pushFunction` which the widget will run in the right time with right data.

We will publish a guide how to integrate few services (like [currently commented out in app.js](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/1626/files#diff-1765d0005076c116a75098c1162e835bR34)).

But I don't understand what you mean by
> to avoid writing again and again the same code?

I don't see issue with repeating code.

> Oh just saw the discussion in #1616. As you guys think 👍

Too fast for me 🚀

> But I don't understand what you mean by
> 
> to avoid writing again and again the same code?
> I don't see issue with repeating code.

Yeah, I was just thinking that those analytics code are always backward compatible and don't change that often; but it's probably fine uncommenting those lines (or recopying those lines) in every single project.

Nice! Can you run with `npm run dev:docs` and ensure:
- the documentation for your widget is added to the documentation page
- the documentation page explains how to connect various analytics projects
?

Thanks a lot

This is really awesome @JanPetr I think this can be a big deal, especially in Magento/Shopify/WooCommerce.

> Yeah, I was just thinking that those analytics code are always backward compatible and don't change that often; but it's probably fine uncommenting those lines (or recopying those lines) in every single project.

I tend to agree with that statement, I would love to have a widget for GA that comes with some sensible defaults.

I would really militate in favor of detecting the global variables that are there and just push the data. That's is the Algolia spirit!

Then if you override some params, you can customize the default behaviour.

WDYT?
@JanPetr Did you manage to write some tests in the end? Otherwise we can put this on our end and do it, no big deal really. Just tell us.

Hey @vvo, in the end I didn't manage to add some. At least I fixed the code according linter and improved docs. If you can take over it'd be great as I'm off since tomorrow.

Thanks!
Will merge this without tests, I won't be able to write them in a timely manner while the feature is here and already working for you.
@JanPetr Thanks a lot for the extra effort on documenting this the proper way and doing all the necessary stuff for releasing a new widget.
